questions.q: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
questions.why: Use 'who' to refer to people.

questions.q: This is the book ___ changed my life.
questions.why: Use 'which' to refer to things.

questions.q: I met a man ___ daughter is a famous singer.
questions.why: 'Whose' shows possession.

questions.q: That's the restaurant ___ we had our first date.
questions.why: 'Where' refers to a place.

questions.q: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
questions.why: 'When' refers to a time.

questions.q: The car ___ is parked outside belongs to my uncle.
questions.why: 'That' can refer to things in a defining clause.

questions.q: My brother, ___ lives in Canada, is visiting next week.
questions.why: In a non-defining clause about a person, use 'who', never 'that'.

questions.q: Paris, ___ is the capital of France, is beautiful in spring.
questions.why: In a non-defining clause about a thing or place, use 'which', not 'that'.

questions.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated as a non-defining clause?
options: My mother who is a nurse works nights.
My mother, who is a nurse, works nights.
My mother, who is a nurse works nights.
My mother who is a nurse, works nights.
questions.answer: My mother, who is a nurse, works nights.
questions.why: Non-defining clauses need a comma before and after the clause.

questions.q: In which sentence can you OMIT the relative pronoun?
options: The man who called you is here.
The book that is on the table is mine.
The film that we watched was boring.
The dog which barks is loud.
questions.answer: The film that we watched was boring.
questions.why: You can omit the pronoun when it is the object of the clause.

questions.q: The person ___ I spoke to was very helpful.
questions.why: 'Who' (or 'whom') refers to a person, even as the object.

questions.q: This is the company for ___ I used to work.
questions.why: After a preposition use 'which' for things, not 'that'.

questions.q: She's the colleague with ___ I share an office.
questions.why: After a preposition, use 'whom' for people in formal English.

questions.q: The reason ___ he left is still a mystery.
questions.why: 'Why' introduces a clause that explains a reason.

questions.q: Which sentence is a DEFINING relative clause (no commas needed)?
options: My only sister, who is older, is tall.
The students who passed are happy.
London, which is huge, is busy.
Tom, who I like, is here.
questions.answer: The students who passed are happy.
questions.why: Defining clauses give essential information and take no commas.

questions.q: The house ___ roof is red is for sale.
questions.why: 'Whose' can show possession for things as well as people.

questions.q: Everything ___ glitters is not gold.
questions.why: After words like 'everything', 'that' is preferred over 'which'.

questions.q: He passed the exam, ___ surprised everyone.
questions.why: 'Which' can refer to a whole previous clause in a non-defining clause.

questions.q: The keys ___ I lost yesterday have been found.
questions.why: 'That' refers to things; here it is the object and could even be omitted.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly omits the relative pronoun?
options: The girl lives here is kind.
The song I heard was lovely.
The man stole it ran away.
questions.answer: The song I heard was lovely.
questions.why: The pronoun (object) is dropped: 'the song [that] I heard'.

questions.q: My grandfather, ___ I admire greatly, is ninety.
questions.why: Non-defining clauses about people use 'who(m)', not 'that'.

questions.q: Summer is the season ___ I feel happiest.
questions.why: 'When' refers to a period of time.

questions.q: The hotel ___ we stayed had a wonderful view.
questions.why: 'Where' refers to a place where something happens.

questions.q: The man to ___ you were talking is my teacher.
questions.why: After a preposition, formal English uses 'whom' for people.

questions.q: Type the relative pronoun: 'The student ___ won the prize is my friend.' (subject, person)
questions.why: Use 'who' or 'that' for a person as the subject.

questions.q: Type the relative pronoun: 'I have a friend ___ father is a pilot.' (possession)
questions.why: 'Whose' shows possession.

questions.q: Type the relative adverb: 'This is the village ___ I grew up.' (place)
questions.why: 'Where' refers to a place.

questions.q: Type the relative pronoun for things: 'The phone ___ I bought is broken.' (object, thing)
questions.why: For a thing as the object, use 'that' or 'which' (or omit it).

questions.q: Type the relative adverb: 'I remember the moment ___ I saw her.' (time)
questions.why: 'When' refers to a point in time.

questions.q: Type the pronoun after the preposition: 'The topic about ___ we argued was politics.' (thing, formal)
questions.why: After a preposition, use 'which' for things, not 'that'.
